ic_name: DALI (Digital Addressable Lighting Interface, IEC 62386 via TI SLAA422A)

protocol_overview.type: Half-duplex digital communication composed of forward and backward frames on a 2-wire DC bus, Manchester-encoded at 1200 baud, defined originally in IEC 60929 Annex E and updated in the IEC 62386 multi-part series. Forward frames are 16 bits (1 start + 8-bit address byte + 8-bit data byte + 2 stop bits). Backward frames are 8 bits (1 start + 8-bit data byte + 2 stop bits) and are sent only as a response to a query/memory forward frame.
protocol_overview.role_model: Single control device (master / application controller) initiates every transaction. One or more control gear (slaves — LED drivers, ballasts, etc.) on the bus receive the forward frame and the addressed one(s) act on the command. For query commands, the addressed control gear may answer with a backward frame after a 7×TE..22×TE settling delay.

duplex_per_transport.DALI 2-wire bus: Half-duplex — only one bus participant transmits at any instant; control device sends forward frame, addressed control gear answers (queries only).

protocol_overview.forward_frame_format: 1 start bit + 1 address byte (YAAAAAAB, MSB first) + 1 data byte (MSB first) + 2 stop bits = 16 information bits + framing.
protocol_overview.backward_frame_format: 1 start bit + 1 data byte (MSB first) + 2 stop bits = 8 information bits + framing.
protocol_overview.encoding: Manchester (bi-phase). Logic '1' = LOW-to-HIGH edge inside the bit cell; logic '0' = HIGH-to-LOW edge inside the bit cell (per Figure 1 of SLAA422A). Idle line = HIGH (passive).
protocol_overview.address_byte_layout: YAAAAAAB. Y=0 → short address mode (AAAAAA = 0..63 short address). Y=1 + AAAAAA != 111111 → group address mode (AAAA = group 0..15 in the upper 4 of AAAAAA, lower 2 = 00). Y=1 + AAAAAA = 111111 → broadcast. Special-command addresses use a different pattern (1010xxx1, 1011xxx1, 1100xxx1) and have B implicitly = 1.

data_byte_meaning_by_B_bit.B=0: Direct arc power command. The data byte is the requested arc power level — 0 = OFF, 1..254 = logarithmic dimming codes (level 1 = 0.1% illumination, level 254 = 100% illumination, constant 2.8% step between codes), 255 = MASK (no change).
data_byte_meaning_by_B_bit.B=1: Indirect command. The data byte is a command code (e.g. 0x00 OFF, 0x01 UP, 0x05 RECALL MAX LEVEL, 0x10..0x1F GO TO SCENE 0..15, 0x20 RESET, 0x90 QUERY STATUS, etc.).

iec_parts.IEC 62386-101: General requirements — System (replaces IEC 60929 Annex E system clauses).
iec_parts.IEC 62386-102: General requirements — Control gear (the generic 'driver' protocol).
iec_parts.IEC 62386-201: Particular requirements for fluorescent lamps (device type 0).
iec_parts.IEC 62386-207: Particular requirements for LED modules (device type 6).
iec_parts.IEC 62386-209: Colour control (device type 8) — RGB / tunable white.

functional_requirements.text: Every DALI forward frame shall consist of 1 start bit + 1 address byte (YAAAAAAB, MSB first) + 1 data byte (MSB first) + 2 stop bits, Manchester-encoded at 1200 baud (TE = 416.67 μs).

A DALI backward frame shall consist of 1 start bit + 1 data byte (MSB first) + 2 stop bits, Manchester-encoded at 1200 baud, and shall only be sent by an addressed control gear in response to a query/memory command forward frame.
Bits shall be Manchester-encoded: a logic '1' is a LOW-to-HIGH transition mid-bit and a logic '0' is a HIGH-to-LOW transition mid-bit. The idle bus state shall be HIGH.

The address byte shall be coded YAAAAAAB. Y=0 → short address (AAAAAA = 0..63). Y=1 + AAAAAA != 111111 → group address (AAAA = group 0..15 in the upper bits, lowest two bits of AAAAAA = 00). Y=1 + AAAAAA = 111111 → broadcast.

The B bit of the address byte shall select the payload type: B=0 → direct arc power command (data byte is the arc-power level 0..254 plus MASK 255); B=1 → indirect command (data byte is a command code per the standard supported set).

Arc power level 0 shall mean OFF; levels 1..254 shall map to a logarithmic dimming curve where level 1 = 0.1% illumination, level 254 = 100% illumination, and the difference between successive levels is a constant 2.8%; level 255 (0xFF) shall mean MASK (do not change the actual level).
The control gear shall expose a physical minimum level PHYS_MIN_LEVEL below which the lamp cannot operate. In the TI example PHYS_MIN_LEVEL = 90 (≈ 1.17% PWM duty for the red/green LEDs at 1.6 kHz).

The control gear shall implement the supported indirect command set of Table 3 of SLAA422A: 0x00 OFF, 0x01 UP (200 ms at Fade Rate), 0x02 DOWN (200 ms at Fade Rate), 0x03 STEP UP, 0x04 STEP DOWN, 0x05 RECALL MAX LEVEL, 0x06 RECALL MIN LEVEL, 0x07 STEP DOWN AND OFF, 0x08 ON AND STEP UP, 0x09 ENABLE DAPC SEQUENCE, 0x10..0x1F GO TO SCENE 0..15, 0x20 RESET, 0x21 STORE ACTUAL LEVEL IN DTR, 0x2A..0x2F STORE DTR AS MAX LEVEL..FADE RATE, 0x40..0x4F STORE DTR AS SCENE 0..15, 0x50..0x5F REMOVE FROM SCENE 0..15, 0x60..0x6F ADD TO GROUP 0..15, 0x70..0x7F REMOVE FROM GROUP 0..15, 0x80 STORE DTR AS SHORT ADDRESS, 0x90..0x9B QUERY commands.

On reception of a query command (e.g. 0x90 QUERY STATUS, 0x91 QUERY BALLAST, 0x92 QUERY LAMP FAILURE, 0x93 QUERY LAMP POWER ON, 0x94 QUERY LIMIT ERROR, 0x95 QUERY RESET STATE, 0x96 QUERY MISSING SHORT ADDRESS, 0x97 QUERY VERSION NUMBER, 0x98 QUERY CONTENT DTR, 0x99 QUERY DEVICE TYPE), the addressed control gear shall transmit a single-byte backward frame 7×TE..22×TE after the end of the forward frame.

Special commands (TERMINATE 0xA1, DTR 0xA3, INITIALIZE 0xA5, RANDOMIZE 0xA7, COMPARE 0xA9, WITHDRAW 0xAB, SEARCH ADDRESS H/M/L 0xB1/0xB3/0xB5, PROGRAM SHORT ADDRESS 0xB7, VERIFY SHORT ADDRESS 0xB9, QUERY SHORT ADDRESS 0xBB, PHYSICAL SELECTION 0xBD, ENABLE DEVICE TYPE X 0xC1, DTR1 0xC3, DTR2 0xC5) are broadcast — every control gear on the bus receives them — and use the upper-nibble pattern 1010/1011/1100 in the address byte to identify them. The data byte carries the command argument.

The control gear shall implement 15 fade times (25 ms..16 s) and 15 fade rates (358 steps/s..2.8 steps/s) controlling the rate of Actual Level transitions to the target arc power. The fastest fade time (25 ms) corresponds to a target update rate of 254 / 0.025 ≈ 10160 levels/s; in the TI implementation the WDT+ interval is ≈ 1 ms (8 MHz / 8192), supporting all fade times but only the fastest fade rates (codes 11..27 in the TI report).
The next forward frame shall not be transmitted until ≥ 22×TE (9.17 ms) after the end of the previous forward frame. A 13.5 ms inter-frame settling time is recommended.

If the forward frame was a query, the backward frame shall begin between 7×TE (2.92 ms) and 22×TE (9.17 ms) after the end of the forward frame. Outside this window the control device shall treat the response as missing.
An address byte with Y=1 and AAAAAA=111111 is broadcast — every control gear on the bus shall act on the command (subject to the command's broadcast semantics). Reads/queries shall not be broadcast.
When Y=1 and the lower 2 bits of AAAAAA are 00, the upper 4 bits of AAAAAA select group 0..15. Every control gear belonging to that group shall act on the command.

Special command INITIALIZE (0xA5) shall place the addressed gear into Configuration Mode for 15 minutes (or until TERMINATE). The data byte of INITIALIZE encodes which gear are selected: 0x00 = all, 0xFF = only gear without short address, otherwise (1AAAAAA0) = specific short address.
Special command RANDOMIZE (0xA7) shall cause every Configuration-Mode gear to generate a fresh 24-bit Random Address.
Special command COMPARE (0xA9) shall cause every Configuration-Mode gear whose Random Address is ≤ Search Address (SEARCH H/M/L registers) to respond with the backward-frame 'YES' code 0xFF.
Special command WITHDRAW (0xAB) shall cause every Configuration-Mode gear whose Random Address equals Search Address to drop out of the addressing iteration.
Special commands SEARCH ADDRESS H (0xB1), M (0xB3), L (0xB5) shall load the 24-bit Search Address used by COMPARE/WITHDRAW. The data byte carries one of the three address bytes (high/middle/low).

Special command PROGRAM SHORT ADDRESS (0xB7) shall write the new short address into the addressed Configuration-Mode gear's persistent store (information memory). Data-byte encoding: 0xFF = delete short address; otherwise 0AAAAAA1 = short address 0..63.
Special command VERIFY SHORT ADDRESS (0xB9) shall cause the gear whose stored short address matches the data byte to answer with the backward-frame 'YES' code 0xFF.

Special command QUERY SHORT ADDRESS (0xBB) shall cause every Configuration-Mode gear whose Random Address equals Search Address to answer with its stored short address (0AAAAAA1 encoding, or 0xFF if none).
Special command TERMINATE (0xA1) shall return the gear to the Normal operating mode and clear the Configuration-Mode flag.

Special command DTR (0xA3) shall load the addressed gear's Data Transfer Register with the data byte. The DTR is used by STORE DTR AS ... indirect commands (0x2A..0x2F, 0x40..0x4F, 0x80, 0xE4) and by READ/WRITE MEMORY LOCATION.

Optional indirect commands beyond the supported set include STORE DTR AS FAST FADE TIME 0xE4, READ MEMORY LOCATION 0xC5, and the query-continued ranges 0xA0..0xAA, 0xF0..0xFF. Unsupported commands shall be silently ignored — there is no NACK frame in DALI.

DALI commands 129 (Enable Write Memory) and 275 (Write Memory Location) are not supported by the TI example because the bank-1 memory map is not implemented; commands 224..227 (Reference System Power, Enable/Disable Current Protector, Select Dimming Curve) are also not supported. Command 240 (QUERY EXTENDED VERSION NUMBER family) must indicate these features are not supported.
Forward frames that violate Manchester encoding, framing (start + 16 data + 2 stop), or fall inside the 22×TE settling window shall be silently discarded by the control gear — DALI has no NACK.

error_response_conditions: Bus voltage out of range (< 9.5 V) → control gear holds Actual Level frozen and shall not respond; will resume on bus recovery.
Manchester encoding violated inside the forward frame → silent discard.
Forward frame with incorrect number of bits (not 16) or missing stop bits → silent discard.
Forward frame received within < 22×TE of the previous frame → silent discard (line still in settling window).
Query command but address does not match this gear's short address / group membership / broadcast → no backward frame transmitted.
Two control gear answer simultaneously to a query (collision in the 7..22 TE window) → both drive the bus, response is corrupted; control device shall treat as 'no valid response'.
Lamp failure detected by the control gear → Actual Level represents the virtual power level; QUERY LAMP FAILURE 0x92 returns 0xFF.
Limit error (e.g. requested level outside Min/Max Level) → QUERY LIMIT ERROR 0x94 returns 0xFF.
Power-up before configuration variables are valid → control gear loads RAM from flash (information memory) per Table 2; if Power On Level is invalid the gear remains OFF.
Unsupported command code (commands 129, 224..227, 242..251 per Table 4) → silently ignored.
compliance_requirements: Bus voltage shall be 11.5 V..22.5 V (per the TI report; the IEC standard window is 9.5 V..22.5 V).
Bus current shall not exceed 250 mA.
Baud rate shall be 1200 ± 10% — half-bit TE = 416.67 μs.
Manchester encoding shall be used for both forward and backward frames.
Forward frame length shall be exactly 16 information bits (1 start + 8 address + 8 data) plus 2 stop bits.
Backward frame length shall be exactly 8 information bits (1 start + 8 data) plus 2 stop bits.
Backward frame shall start between 7×TE and 22×TE after the end of the matching forward frame.
Next forward frame shall not start sooner than 22×TE after the end of the previous forward frame.
Address byte format shall be YAAAAAAB; special-command and configuration-command address bytes shall follow the upper-nibble patterns 1010/1011/1100 per IEC 62386-102.
Arc power level 0 = OFF; 1..254 = logarithmic curve (0.1%..100%, 2.8% step); 255 = MASK.
DALI commands shall be silently ignored when not supported — there is no NACK frame.

Persistent variables (Power On Level, System Failure Level, Min/Max Level, Fade Rate/Time, Short Address, Group 0..7 + 8..15, Scene 0..15, Random Address, Fast Fade Time, Failure Status, Operating Mode, Dimming Curve) shall be stored in non-volatile memory and restored on power-up.
